content: The Magnificent Mei and Friends comic series and its accompanying Teacher’s Guide were developed as part of the Helping Adolescents Thrive (HAT) initiative, a collaborative effort by the World Health Organization (WHO) Departments of Mental Health and Substance Use, Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health and Ageing, and UNICEF’s Health Section. This initiative aims to promote and protect adolescent mental health. The development team included Joanna Lai (UNICEF), Sarah Watts (Australia), Tanvi Jain (UNICEF), Batool Fatima (WHO), Chiara Servili (WHO), and Tarun Dua (WHO). The comic illustrations were created by Aizat Zhunusova. Collaborators included Bhawana Shrestha and Sagar Satyal from My Emotions Matter in Nepal, Gunjan Dhonju from Kanti Children’s Hospital in Nepal, Jackie Stewart and Sarah Skeen from Stellenbosch University in South Africa, Mohammed Amin Zurak from the University of Ghana Medical Centre, and Sagun Ballav Pant from Tribhuvan University in Nepal. Reviewers included experts from WHO, UNICEF, and other organizations across various countries. The materials were designed to support social and emotional learning (SEL) among adolescents, aiming to enhance psychosocial well-being, prevent mental health conditions, and reduce risky behaviors. SEL is defined as the process through which individuals acquire and apply knowledge, skills, and attitudes to manage emotions, develop healthy identities, show empathy, maintain supportive relationships, and make responsible decisions. The Teacher’s Guide is intended for use by educators, school counselors, and mental health professionals working with adolescents aged 10–14 years. It provides background information on mental health, strategies for effective communication with adolescents, and guidance on supporting students in seeking additional help when needed. The guide also includes classroom lesson plans and activities that align with the comic series, which presents relatable real-life scenarios to engage young adolescents. The materials emphasize that mental health is a critical component of overall well-being and is as important as physical health. Teachers are uniquely positioned to help students develop social and emotional skills, which are essential for navigating school, relationships, and life challenges. Adolescence is a pivotal period for mental health intervention, as half of all mental health conditions begin before the age of 14. The guide is not a substitute for professional psychological care or treatment. Teachers are encouraged to refer adolescents to appropriate mental health or social care services if they identify serious concerns, such as suicidal ideation, existing mental health conditions, or experiences of abuse or exploitation. The initiative also seeks to dispel common myths about mental health, such as the misconception that mental illness is a sign of weakness or that it only affects certain groups. Mental health conditions can affect anyone, regardless of socioeconomic status or life circumstances. Recognizing the need for help and seeking support requires strength and courage. The materials highlight the importance of supporting parents and caregivers, as they play a crucial role in the growth, development, and recovery of adolescents with mental health conditions. Factors such as poverty, violence, and adverse life events can influence adolescent mental health, and it is essential to provide a supportive environment for both adolescents and their families.
